e: An AVE train travelling from Madrid to Barcelona catches fire at Ricla, forcing the evacuation of all 283 passengers on board.
Prime Minister Sanchez calls a snap election for 29 November after the Congress of Deputies fails to pass proposed legislation on housing.
A bar collapses in San Vicente de la Sonsierra, La Rioja, injuring 11 people.
A right-wing demonstration in Madrid over the 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis draws tens of thousands of people.

Eighty-seven year old pensioner Maricarmen Abascal is forcibly evicted from her rented apartment of 70 years in Madrid after being unable to pay increased payments, triggering the 2026 Spanish housing protests.
The Congress of Deputies approves legislation granting Spanish citizenship to Sahrawis born under the Spanish administration of Western Sahara.
A boat carrying migrants is discovered adrift off Gran Canaria. At least five deaths are recorded.
The government reverses its policy for unaccompanied Moroccan migrant children in Ceuta, allowing about 500 children to relocate to peninsular Spain.
A magnitude 4.9 earthquake hits Granada, injuring three people.

A total solar eclipse occurs at the Moon's descending node of the orbit in North America and Europe. The total eclipse passes over the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic Ocean, northeastern Portugal and northern Spain.
Spain suspends Schengen Area agreements with Italy for one month in response to similar measures imposed by the latter country over the 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident.
Thousands of migrants enter the enclave city of Ceuta from its border with Morocco. At least 34 people die in the process.
Italy suspends Schengen Area agreements with Spain, citing the 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident.
One person is killed by a collapsed fountain in Ciudad Rodrigo during celebrations over the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
Spain wins the 2026 FIFA World Cup after defeating Argentina 1–0 at the final.
The border fence separating Spain and Gibraltar is removed as part of a treaty with the United Kingdom placing Gibraltar under the Schengen Area.
Twelve people are killed in a wildfire in Almeria Province.
Two people are killed while four others are injured in a fire at a residential building in Magaluf.
The central tower of the Sagrada Familia in Barcelona is officially blessed by Pope Leo XIV.
Pope Leo XIV arrives in Spain as part of a seven-day visit.

The municipal government of La Línea de la Concepción cancels a scheduled warmup football match on 9 June between Chile and DR Congo ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, citing possible health risks amid the 2026 Central Africa Ebola epidemic.
Two people are killed while four others are injured in a mass shooting in El Ejido, Andalusia.

Two people are arrested in El Ejido, Andalusia in connection with the seizure in Germany of eight metric tons of cocaine valued at 500 million euros ($582 million) from a container that originated from West Africa in February.
A tourist bus falls off a ravine in La Gomera, killing one person and injuring 27 others.

Spanish police dismantle a hashish-smuggling operation involving an underground tunnel linking Morocco to Ceuta; authorities seize 17 metric tons of hashish, €1.4 million in cash, and arrest 27 people.
The Spanish government closes the country's airspace to U.S. planes involved in attacks on Iran.

Noelia Castillo euthanasia case: A 25-year-old woman from Barcelona undergoes euthanasia after her request was approved by authorities and upheld through multiple legal challenges despite opposition from her family.
King Felipe VI issues an acknowledgement of abuses made by Spanish conquistadors during the colonization of the Americas in remarks made at the National Archaeological Museum in Madrid.
Spain permanently withdraws its ambassador to Israel and terminates the position after a worsening of bilateral diplomatic relations.
The Government of Spain announces that the frigate Cristóbal Colón will join French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle and Greek Navy ships to the protection and aerial defence of Cyprus.
U.S. military aircraft begin to leave Spain after the Spanish government denied the U.S. permission to use their airbases for military operations against Iran.
The government unveils the "Spain Grows" fund, a public investment fund aimed at raising 120 billion euros ($142 billion) to help ease an ongoing housing crisis.
Five people are killed in a fire at an apartment in Manlleu.
The Sindicato Español de Maquinistas y Ayudantes Ferroviarios starts a strike following the train derailments in Adamuz, Córdoba, and Gelida, Catalonia.
One person is reported missing in Málaga Province after falling into the Turvilla river during heavy rains caused by Storm Leonardo.
The government announces amendments to immigration laws granting unauthorized migrants (potentially 500,000 migrants) legal residency of up to one year along with work permits.
A commuter train collides with a crane near Cartagena, injuring four people.
A Rodalies de Catalunya train collides with a retaining wall that had fallen on the track in Gelida, killing the driver and injuring 37 passengers.
Two high-speed trains derail and collide near Adamuz, killing 43 people.

A Turkish Airlines aircraft flying from Istanbul makes an emergency landing at Barcelona-El Prat Airport following a bomb threat involving a passenger creating an in-flight wireless network with a suspicious title.
